name: Colorado
sources: CO DOR, 2026 Form DR 0104EP Estimated Tax Worksheet line 2: 'Estimated 2026 Colorado income tax - 4.4% of line 1' (tax.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/DR_0104EP_2026.pdf)

CO DOR, 2025 Book 104 (tax.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/Book104_2025.pdf): line 1 is federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15); line 4 addback of the federal standard or itemized deduction above $12,000 (single, head of household, married filing separately) / $16,000 (joint) when federal AGI exceeds $300,000; line 3 QBI addback above $500,000 / $1,000,000 AGI

CO DOR, Individual Income Tax Guide, January 2026 (tax.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/Individual_Income_Tax_Guide_January_2026.pdf): rate 4.25% (2024), 4.4% (2025); deduction addback limits fall to $1,000 single / $2,000 joint for 2026 and later; overtime deduction added back from 2026; no addback for qualified tips
provisional: The 4.4% rate is the 2026 statutory rate used on the 2026 estimated-tax worksheet; a temporary TABOR rate reduction for 2026, if the state's revenue certification triggers one, is not reflected
notes: When federal AGI is over $300,000, Colorado adds back nearly all of the federal standard or itemized deduction (all but $1,000 single / $2,000 joint) and, above $500,000 / $1,000,000, the QBI deduction; this estimate does not, so it is low for those households.
Colorado's pension and Social Security subtraction for retirees and the TABOR refund are not included.
